decks.domain: Railroad crossing cautions, highway route markers and mile posts, work zones, work-zone devices and fines, flaggers, and pavement markings

cards.front: What should you never try to do with a train at a crossing?
cards.back: Never try to race a train or any other on-track equipment to a crossing.

cards.front: Which vehicles should you expect to stop at railroad crossings?
cards.back: Expect buses and gasoline tankers to stop at railroad crossings, because those vehicles are required to stop there.

cards.front: Why be ready for the vehicle ahead to stop at a railroad crossing?
cards.back: Buses and gasoline tankers must stop at railroad crossings, so be ready for the vehicle ahead of you to stop there.

cards.front: At night, what should you watch for at railroad crossings?
cards.back: When driving at night, watch for railroad crossing warning signs that may not be lit.

cards.front: Which route markers appear on highway guide signs?
cards.back: Highway guide signs include route markers for interstate routes, national routes and state routes.

cards.front: What makes Arizona one of only a few states with its highway markers?
cards.back: Arizona is one of only a few states that has mileage markers on every state highway.

cards.front: How far off the right shoulder do Arizona mile posts stand?
cards.back: Arizona mile posts stand two feet off the right shoulder of the highway.

cards.front: About how far apart are Arizona mile posts?
cards.back: Arizona mile posts are placed about one mile apart.

cards.front: Which mile post number is an offset and which is a spacing?
cards.back: A mile post sits two feet off the right shoulder, and the posts are spaced about one mile apart, so one number is an offset and the other is a spacing.

cards.front: How can a nearby mile post help you after a crash or breakdown?
cards.back: A nearby mile post lets you tell others where you are after a crash, a mechanical problem or running out of gas.

cards.front: If you must stop on a highway, what should you note?
cards.back: If you have to stop on a highway, note which route you are on and roughly how far you are from a mile post.

decks.domain: Railroad crossing cautions, highway route markers and mile posts, work zones, work-zone devices and fines, flaggers, and pavement markings

cards.front: What two kinds of work zones does the manual describe?
cards.back: A work zone can be a long-term project with permanent signs or a temporary site with portable signs that stays up for only a few hours.

cards.front: How do long-term and temporary work zones differ in their signs?
cards.back: A long-term work zone uses permanent signs, while a temporary work area uses portable signs that may stay up for only a few hours.

cards.front: What are the typical work-zone crashes?
cards.back: Typical work-zone crashes are rear-end collisions from drivers going too fast, collisions with fixed objects, and vehicles striking the people working there.

cards.front: How should you drive in a work zone?
cards.back: In a work zone, stay on high alert and be ready to slow or stop suddenly for changing conditions, including a change in the road surface.

cards.front: Where may workers and construction vehicles be in a work zone?
cards.back: Workers and construction vehicles may be right beside the travel lanes or may enter them at any point in the work zone.

cards.front: Whom do work-zone alerting and controlling devices protect and guide?
cards.back: The alerting and controlling devices used in construction and maintenance areas protect highway workers as well as guiding drivers and pedestrians.

cards.front: What is the basic color of road construction warning devices?
cards.back: Orange is the basic color of the warning devices used in road construction and maintenance areas.

cards.front: What three things must you do at every construction site?
cards.back: At every construction site you must drive slowly, stay especially alert and obey the posted speed limit.

cards.front: Whom does a work-zone speed limit protect?
cards.back: A work-zone speed limit protects the workers doing the job as well as the drivers passing through.

cards.front: What happens to a speeding fine in a work zone when signs are posted?
cards.back: When work-zone signs are posted, the fine for a speeding violation there is doubled.

cards.front: When does the doubled work-zone fine apply?
cards.back: The doubled fine described for work zones applies to a speed violation when the work-zone signs are posted.

decks.domain: Railroad crossing cautions, highway route markers and mile posts, work zones, work-zone devices and fines, flaggers, and pavement markings

cards.front: What do flaggers do in road work zones?
cards.back: Flaggers are used in road work zones to stop traffic, slow it down or guide it safely through.

cards.front: What do flaggers wear, and how do they direct traffic?
cards.back: Flaggers wear orange vests or jackets and direct traffic with red flags or stop and slow panels.

cards.front: What do construction and maintenance signs warn of?
cards.back: Construction and maintenance signs warn drivers of possible danger in or near a work area.

cards.front: What shape are most signs in highway and street work areas?
cards.back: Most of the signs used in highway and street work areas are diamond-shaped.

cards.front: What do flashing arrow panels warn you of?
cards.back: Flashing arrow panels are used both day and night to warn you early that you must move left or right into another lane.

cards.front: What should you do when you see a flashing arrow panel?
cards.back: When you see a flashing arrow panel, slow down and get ready to merge in the direction the arrow points.

cards.front: What can electronic message signs warn you about?
cards.back: Electronic message signs on some roads give advance warning of construction zones, special traffic directions, road closures or weather conditions.

cards.front: What do cones, drums and barricades do?
cards.back: Cones, drums and barricades alert you and guide you safely through a work area, and at night they may carry warning lights.

cards.front: How does a flagger differ from a flashing arrow panel?
cards.back: A flagger is a person in orange who stops, slows or guides traffic, while a flashing arrow panel is a lighted board that tells you to merge.

cards.front: How does a flashing arrow panel differ from an electronic message sign?
cards.back: A flashing arrow panel asks you to change lanes in the arrow's direction, while an electronic message sign gives advance information such as closures, special directions or weather.

cards.front: How do work-zone signs differ from cones, drums and barricades?
cards.back: Construction and maintenance signs warn of danger near the work area, while cones, drums and barricades guide you through the work area itself.

decks.domain: Railroad crossing cautions, highway route markers and mile posts, work zones, work-zone devices and fines, flaggers, and pavement markings

cards.front: What do pavement markings do?
cards.back: Pavement markings guide and warn drivers and also regulate traffic.

cards.front: What colors are pavement markings, and what about combinations?
cards.back: Pavement markings are either yellow or white, they can be combined, and each combination carries its own meaning.

cards.front: What do yellow center lines tell you?
cards.back: Yellow center lines tell you that traffic on the road flows in both directions.

cards.front: What do white lines separate and mark?
cards.back: White lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and also mark the road edge, stop lines and pedestrian crosswalks.

cards.front: How do yellow lines differ from white lines?
cards.back: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions, while white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction.

cards.front: What does a broken yellow line allow, and why take care?
cards.back: A broken yellow line lets you pass on the left when the road is clear, but because you face oncoming traffic you must pass with extreme caution.

cards.front: What does a broken yellow line beside a solid yellow line mean?
cards.back: Where a broken yellow line runs beside a solid yellow line, passing is allowed in only one direction.

cards.front: When may you pass where the broken yellow line is on your side?
cards.back: If the broken yellow line is on your side, you may pass once the road ahead is clear.
cards.memory_hook: broken on your side, may pass

cards.front: May you pass when the solid yellow line is nearest your lane?
cards.back: Passing is not allowed when the solid yellow line is the one nearest your lane.

cards.front: How does the line on your side decide whether you may pass?
cards.back: With a broken yellow line on your side you may pass when the road is clear, but with a solid yellow line on your side you may not pass.

cards.front: What do double solid yellow lines allow you to do?
cards.back: Double solid yellow lines ban passing in both directions, and you may cross them only to make a left turn.

cards.front: How do double solid yellow lines differ from broken white lines?
cards.back: Double solid yellow lines may be crossed only to turn left, while broken white lines may be crossed with caution to change lanes after signaling.
cards.memory_hook: left turn only versus lane change

decks.domain: Railroad crossing cautions, highway route markers and mile posts, work zones, work-zone devices and fines, flaggers, and pavement markings

cards.front: When may you cross broken white lines?
cards.back: Broken white lines separate lanes going the same way and may be crossed with caution after you signal your lane change.

cards.front: What do solid white lines mark?
cards.back: Solid white lines mark turn lanes and keep drivers from changing lanes near intersections.

cards.front: How do broken white lines differ from solid white lines?
cards.back: Broken white lines may be crossed with caution, while solid white lines mark turn lanes and keep drivers from changing lanes near intersections.

cards.front: What must you do in a lane marked with a curved arrow and the word ONLY?
cards.back: If your lane shows a curved arrow with the word ONLY, you must turn the way the arrow points.

cards.front: What may you do in a lane with both a curved and a straight arrow?
cards.back: If your lane shows both a curved arrow and a straight arrow, you may either turn that way or go straight.

cards.front: How does an ONLY arrow differ from a combined arrow?
cards.back: A curved arrow with the word ONLY requires the turn, while a lane with a curved arrow and a straight arrow lets you turn or continue straight.

cards.front: What does a bicycle painted on the road warn you of?
cards.back: A bicycle painted on the road warns that bicyclists may be present, so drive with caution.

cards.front: What does a painted curb mean?
cards.back: A painted curb means special rules apply if you want to park there, and each curb color has its own meaning.

recap_hooks.text: Never race a train, expect buses and tankers to stop, and use mile posts two feet off the shoulder, about a mile apart, to report where you are.
In a work zone, drive slowly, stay alert, obey the posted limit, and remember speeding fines double when signs are posted.
Flaggers stop, slow or guide you, arrow panels tell you to merge, and cones, drums and barricades guide you through.
Yellow lines separate opposite directions; pass only with the broken line on your side, and cross double solid yellow only to turn left.
Cross broken white lines after signaling, stay put at solid white lines, and follow your lane arrow.
